assertion: US traffic deaths jumped 10.8% in 2021 to 43,230, the most in a single year since 2005.
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes WHERE "year" IN (2020,2021) GROUP BY "year"

assertion: traffic deaths dropped 2.5% to 16,750 in the first half of the year. It was the lowest number since 2015 and down from 17,175 in the same period last year.
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes WHERE "year" = 2024 GROUP BY "year"
independent_value: NHTSA Table 1: H1 2025 = 8,120+9,055 = 17,175; H1 2015 = 16,193, H1 2019 = 17,025; 16,750/17,175 = -2.5%. 16,750 itself is from NHTSA's H1 release as relayed by Reuters.

assertion: This year is on pace to be the fifth straight year of declines
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes WHERE "year" BETWEEN 2021 AND 2024 GROUP BY "year"

assertion: Full-year traffic deaths for 2025 fell to the lowest number since 2019 and the fatality rate fell to 1.10 fatalities per 100 million vehicle miles traveled, the second-lowest yearly figure in US history
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes WHERE "year" = 2019 GROUP BY "year"

assertion: One area of concern remains bicyclist deaths, which rose 4% to 1,148 last year.
independent_value: NHTSA final 2024 pedalcyclist deaths 1,103 (2023: 1,173); 1,148/1,103 = +4.1%, consistent. 1,148 itself not found in an NHTSA release.
